claims.claim_ar: الاستفهام الإنكاري/التوبيخي في عبارة «أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ كَثْرَتُكُمْ...» لإدانة الاعتماد على كثرتهم وعدم انتفاعهم بها
claims.claim_en: Use of the interrogative for reproach/condemnation in 'أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ كَثْرَتُكُمْ...' to blame reliance on numerical superiority that proved useless.
claims.rhetorical_effect: creates reproachful tone, sharpens admonition and undermines the addressees' pride

claims.claim_ar: تكرار جذر ك-ث-ر في «مَوَاطِنَ كَثِيرَةٍ» و«كَثْرَتُكُمْ» كوسيلة بلاغية لتوكيد المعنى
claims.claim_en: Repetition of the root k‑th‑r in 'مَوَاطِنَ كَثِيرَةٍ' and 'كَثْرَتُكُمْ' as a rhetorical repetition to reinforce the idea of multitude.
claims.rhetorical_effect: intensifies the notion of multiplicity and thereby heightens the contrast with the subsequent ineffectiveness of that multiplicity

claims.claim_ar: مقابلة/تباين بين نعمة النصرة في مَوَاطِنَ كَثِيرَةٍ ثم ضيق الأرض عليهم وولّيتهم؛ أي تباين بين النصر ثم الفشل والهزيمة
claims.claim_en: Antithesis/contrast (tibaq) between God's granting many victories and then the earth constricting and them turning away — a movement from triumph to failure.
claims.needs_review_reason: The supporting source text shows comparative/contrastive phrasing elsewhere; linking it as explicit evidence for this ayah's antithesis is interpretive and may need a direct commentary on S9:25.
claims.rhetorical_effect: produces striking reversal: what seemed like advantage becomes ineffective, amplifying the moral lesson about reliance on God rather than numbers

warnings: Source chunks provided are general lexicon and commentary excerpts; few chunks directly discuss S9:25. Claims tie ayah phenomena to related rhetorical observations in the chunks—some mappings are interpretive and flagged in 'needs_review_reason'.

Some claims (especially antithesis/tibaq) rely on thematic parallelism rather than an explicit, dedicated statement about this specific ayah in the supplied excerpts—please review against primary tafsir/بلاغة texts for confirmation.
